entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bodhiruci (菩提流支, c. 450–535 CE), an influential Indian Buddhist monk, arrived in China during the Northern Wei dynasty, becoming a pivotal figure in the transmission and localization of Mahayana Buddhism. Arriving in Luoyang in 508 CE, he spent decades translating Sanskrit scriptures into Chinese, profoundly shaping the intellectual and spiritual landscape of early medieval China. His work facilitated the integration of complex Indian philosophical concepts into Chinese thought, establishing a critical foundation for the development of indigenous Buddhist schools and contributing to the global spread of Buddhist teachings during the Classical era.

Bodhiruci's most significant achievement was his prolific translation work at the White Horse Temple (Baima Si) in Luoyang. He is credited with translating at least 39 texts in 127 fascicles, most notably the *Dasabhumika Sutra* (十地經論), a commentary on the 'Ten Stages' chapter of the *Avatamsaka Sutra*. This translation, completed around 511 CE, became the foundational text for the Dilun school (地論宗), which emphasized the bodhisattva path and the stages of spiritual attainment. He also translated the *Lankavatara Sutra* (入楞伽經), a text central to the early development of Chan (Zen) Buddhism, and the *Vimalakirti Sutra* (維摩詰經), making these profound philosophical works accessible to a wider Chinese audience and fostering deep engagement with their doctrines.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bodhiruci's extensive translation work, particularly of the *Dasabhumika Sutra*, directly led to the formation of the Dilun school and laid critical groundwork for the later Huayan school, profoundly shaping the intellectual and religious landscape of Chinese Buddhism for centuries.
